questions.question: You are defending alone near your goal. The central route is open and no teammate can cover it. What should you protect?
options: The route toward the middle of your goal
The route toward the sideline first
Only the attacker's strongest foot
The space behind the attacker
questions.explanation: Protect the direct route to goal and try to delay or guide play wider. A team pressing plan may use a different direction when cover is ready.

questions.question: What does 'pressure' mean in defending?
options: Reduce the ball carrier's time and space
Stand close to a teammate instead of the ball
Wait at the goal line for every attack
Attempt a tackle from any distance
questions.explanation: Close the space quickly, then slow down under control. You want to limit the next action without being easily dribbled past.

questions.question: Who usually starts pressure when the team has cover behind?
options: The nearest player who can reach the ball carrier
The deepest player, leaving the back line
The goalkeeper, regardless of distance
The fastest player, regardless of position
questions.explanation: The nearest player able to press usually goes first. Teammates must cover behind and protect passing lanes.

questions.question: If your teammate is pressuring the ball, what should you do?
options: Cover space or open players
Stand flat beside the first defender
Run away from the passing lane
Press the same side and leave cover open
questions.explanation: You're the second line-block passes or be ready if they get beat.

questions.question: In zonal defending, an attacker moves out of your area. What should you do?
options: Communicate and adjust with teammates while watching the next threat
Follow that attacker anywhere on the field
Stop watching them as soon as they leave the area
Remain on one spot even when play moves
questions.explanation: A zone is a responsibility, not a fixed spot. Track threats, pass on information, and move together with the ball.

questions.question: Why is talking important on defense?
options: To organize and warn teammates
To distract from your own marking
To call for pressure after the pass is gone
To make every defender chase the ball
questions.explanation: Call out danger, help teammates know who to mark or when to press.

questions.question: What does staying 'compact' mean?
options: Keep useful distances between teammates and lines
Have every defender stand beside the ball
Put the entire team on the goal line
Keep the same gaps regardless of the ball
questions.explanation: Compact teams leave fewer useful gaps for opponents. Keep enough space to cover one another without all chasing the same player.

questions.question: An attacker takes a heavy touch. When should you try to win the ball?
options: When you can reach it safely and under control
Whenever the touch looks heavy, even from far away
Only after the attacker has regained control
By lunging through the player to reach it
questions.explanation: A heavy touch can create a chance to tackle, but distance, balance, and safety still matter.

questions.question: Where should a weak-side defender (far from the ball) be?
options: Shift toward the middle to help cover
Stay wide by themselves
Stand on the goalpost instead of marking
Stay outside the defensive shape
questions.explanation: Stay tucked in to help defend passes and protect the middle.

questions.question: A low cross is coming in. Your teammate can challenge for it, and you see a runner behind them. What should you do?
options: Track the runner and cover the space behind your teammate
Join the same challenge and leave the runner
Watch the ball without checking the runner
Move toward the corner taker
questions.explanation: Defenders need different jobs. One may attack the ball while another protects a runner or space behind. Communicate who has each job.

questions.question: What does it mean to be 'goal-side'?
options: Stand between the attacker and our goal
Stand behind your teammate
Stand near their net
Stand in the corner
questions.explanation: It helps stop shots or passes toward our goal.

questions.question: What does 'jockeying' mean in defense?
options: Stay in front and slow them down
Dive in from too far away
Turn and sprint away from pressure
Let the attacker pick their route
questions.explanation: It's a way to delay them without diving in-just stay in control!

questions.question: When facing a dribbler, where should your attention be?
options: The ball and the attacker's movement, with quick checks of nearby danger
Only their face and eyes
Only your own feet
Only your teammate behind you
questions.explanation: Watch the ball and body movement without staring at just one detail. Brief checks help you notice support and runners.

questions.question: What does 'clear your lines' mean?
options: Kick it out of danger
Pass softly into central pressure
Dribble across your own goal
Wait for attackers to close you down
questions.explanation: Sometimes you just need to get the ball away from our goal!

questions.question: Why is teamwork important on defense?
options: Everyone helps and covers each other
One player can chase while others watch
Only one player defends
It lets weak-side defenders stay wide
questions.explanation: Defense works best when players help, cover, and trust each other.

questions.question: If you cannot win the ball right away, what is still a good defensive job?
options: Slow the attacker down
Dive in from far away
Let them run centrally
Stop recovering goal-side
questions.explanation: Delaying the attacker gives teammates time to recover and get organized.

questions.question: Why should defenders protect the middle first?
options: The middle usually leads to the easiest shots
The sideline is the only danger
It saves running
The middle is never used
questions.explanation: Shots from central areas are dangerous, so defenders try to force play wide.

questions.question: Your teammate presses and is beaten. You were covering behind. What now?
options: Become the next defender to delay while they recover
Stay behind them even as the attacker advances
Rush at the attacker from too far away
Leave the middle to mark a distant player
questions.explanation: Pressure and cover roles change as the ball moves. Delay under control so the beaten teammate has time to recover.

questions.question: When defending near your own goal, what kind of clearance is best?
options: High or wide away from danger
Soft into the middle
Back across your own goal
Straight to an attacker
questions.explanation: Clearances should move the ball away from the most dangerous central space.

questions.question: After your team wins the ball back, what should defenders do?
options: Open up to support the first pass
All sprint away from the ball
Stay marked behind opponents
Stop supporting once the ball is won
questions.explanation: Good defenders help the team keep possession after winning it.

questions.question: A pressing forward curves their run so an opponent cannot pass to midfield. What are they using?
options: Their approach angle to block a lane while pressuring the ball
Only their speed to chase the ball
A rule that prevents the midfielder from moving
A man-marking job on two distant players
questions.explanation: The space screened behind a pressing player is often called a cover shadow. The presser can limit a passing lane without standing next to that receiver.

questions.question: Your team plans to press a backward pass. Why must players behind the first presser move too?
options: To close the next options and cover space left by the press
To surround the same ball carrier with every player
To stand still so the team shape is unchanged
To leave every far-side receiver free
questions.explanation: A pressing trigger is a cue to act together. One player starts pressure while others make the next pass difficult and protect against being played through.

questions.question: Your back line is high, but the opponent on the ball is unpressured and can pass behind. What is a warning sign?
options: The passer has time to find a runner behind your line
All high defensive lines are always unsafe
The nearest attacker is standing still
Your team has more total possession
questions.explanation: The defensive line and pressure on the ball must work together. With no pressure, defenders may need to drop and track runs rather than blindly hold a high line.

questions.question: You are defending a 2v1 and help is recovering. What is often the priority?
options: Delay while protecting the most dangerous route and adjusting to the ball
Sprint at the ball from a distance and hope to win it immediately
Mark the receiver tightly and let the ball carrier run straight at goal
Stay on the goal line regardless of where the ball is
questions.explanation: You cannot remove every option alone. Delaying and shaping the attack can buy time, while a poorly timed lunge can leave both attackers free.

questions.question: A far-side winger stays wide while your team defends on the opposite side. How do you balance the threats?
options: Tuck in to protect the middle while checking the winger and preparing for a switch
Ignore the winger until they receive
Stay at the far touchline regardless of central danger
Follow the ball all the way to the opposite touchline
questions.explanation: Being compact does not mean forgetting the far side. Scan, communicate, and adjust as a switch becomes possible.
